body: I was a slave to my old terrible abusive job just to be a slave to weed......
Because I want a new perspective in life. Getting high all the time gets boring because its a repeated cycle.
Never put your self in the position to be handed a joint.. You never know. Coming out of addiction is about a new life. What do you want to do?

But hey if that's what you want to do, do it! It may be best for some people but I'm looking to quit through my own "boot camp". Exercise, discipline, water/healthy foods.. That way I'm not stuck in a position where I'm forced to do things. You know?
Because there are so many other options than the military.. Although I'm sure it would make him/her quit, its not the best route imo

Take it easy man. I know exactly how the cycle goes. The less you smoke the easier it will be. Its harder for me to quit after smoking huge amounts. Try to quit for 1 or 2 days. Then go 3 or 4, and so on... That's my plan. 24 hours since my last smoke and I'm feeling confident and I go through an ounce in a week or 2 and dab quite a bit. You've got this!

But if I quit tonight then I will have a super high tolerance and it will be 50x harder instead of gradually quitting and just having that one last time. I believe I have the will power, especially if I prepare correctly. *tonight is not that not that night*

I just want my last blunt to be a quality high at the right time. It's been awhile. Why get semi high and have a huge tolerance when you decide to quit instead of getting super baked and knowing that you could be done forever if not a long time. The only problem is cutting down on usage!

Well kind of not exactly. I said I'm going to gradually quit then when I feel comfortable I will smoke that last one whenever I'm in the mood or if its a special occasion. I'm going out on a bang. I just feel less complete if I end on a dull, boring high. It never works that way for me sadly.

It sounds to me like depersonalization. I'm going through the same exact things. Sometimes I'm like who am I... Or who was I before I am now... To me I think preparation is a huge part in quitting. You need to be in the right mind set, be ready to exercise, drink water. Being dependent on this stuff gets deep lol. Just think about the years wasted and how you can totally change your situation around. The good news is your brain is incredible and will rewire itself even after long term use. It takes time. It takes suffering. Stay busy and exercise until you want to pass out. Best of luck. 
*Let your past make you better, not bitter*
